t: Hong Kong - Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution
body: Exercise increased caution when traveling to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) due to the a rbitrary enforcement of local laws.
Exercise increased caution due to the arbitrary enforcement of local laws .

• Hong Kong SAR authorities have passed laws that limit people’s civil liberties. The laws apply to anyone in Hong Kong, including foreigners. Authorities have also issued arrest warrants for individuals, including U.S. citizens, located outside of Hong Kong for activities undertaken overseas.
• U.S. government employees must follow the policies established by their Department or Agency regarding official or personal travel to China, including to Hong Kong SAR.
National security laws and restriction of civil liberties
Since 2020, Hong Kong SAR authorities have taken away many freedoms from people living there.

On June 30, 2020, China imposed the Law on Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong SAR. On March 23, 2024, Hong Kong passed another similar law. Both laws list many crimes that are vaguely defined. The crimes include:
• Trying to break apart China (acts of secession)
• Working against the government (subversion)
• Terrorism
• Working with other countries against China (collusion with foreign entities)
• Betraying the country (treason)
• Stealing government secrets
• Insurrection
• Sabotage against public infrastructure
• External interference

On March 23, 2026, the Hong Kong government changed the implementing rules relating to the Hong Kong National Security Law. It is now a criminal offense in national security cases to refuse to give the Hong Kong police passwords or not assist in decryption to allow authorities full access to all personal electronic devices, including cellphones and laptops.

This legal change applies to everyone, including U.S. citizens, in Hong Kong, upon arrival, or just transiting Hong Kong International Airport. In addition, the Hong Kong government also has more authority to take and keep any personal devices, as evidence, that they claim are linked to national security offenses.

China applies its national security laws to everyone in Hong Kong SAR, including foreigners. China may also attempt to apply these laws to people who do not live in Hong Kong – including U.S. citizens and permanent residents.
If you say anything critical about China or Hong Kong SAR, you could be arrested, detained, kicked out, or prosecuted.

Hong Kong SAR authorities have issued arrest warrants for people who live in other countries and are alleged to be violating these laws. This includes U.S. citizens and permanent residents living outside their jurisdiction. Hong Kong SAR authorities are offering cash rewards to anyone who gives information that helps them arrest these people if they come to Hong Kong SAR.
Dual nationality

The Hong Kong SAR government does not recognize dual nationality. Dual U.S.-Chinese citizens and U.S. citizens of Chinese descent may be subject to additional security procedures and harassment. If you are a dual U.S.-Chinese citizen and enter Hong Kong SAR on a U.S. passport, and you are detained or arrested, Chinese authorities must notify the U.S. Embassy or a U.S. Consulate General of your detention. They must allow U.S. consular officials to have access to you.

Even if you enter on a U.S. passport, U.S. consular officers may not have access to you. For more information, visit Consular Protection and Right of Abode in HK(SAR) for Dual Nationals – U.S. Consulate General Hong Kong & Macau .
Demonstrations

Participating in demonstrations or other activities that authorities interpret as constituting an act of secession, subversion, terrorism, or collusion with a foreign country could result in criminal charges under the 2020 Hong Kong National Security Law, the 2024 Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, or other legal provisions. Be aware of your surroundings and avoid demonstrations.
body_zh: 由于任意执行当地法律，在前往香港特别行政区（特区）时更加谨慎。
由于任意执行当地法律，因此要更加谨慎。
• 香港特别行政区当局通过了限制人民公民自由的法律。这些法律适用于香港的任何人，包括外国人。当局还对在香港境外从事海外活动的个人（包括美国公民）发出逮捕令。
• 美国政府雇员必须遵守其部门或机构制定的有关前往中国（包括香港特别行政区）的公务或个人旅行的政策。
国家安全法和限制公民自由
自2020年以来，香港特别行政区当局剥夺了居住在那里的人的许多自由。
2020年6月30日，中国实施了《香港特别行政区国家安全保障法》。2024年3月23日，香港通过了另一项类似的法律。这两部法律都列出了许多定义模糊的罪行。这些罪行包括：
• 试图分裂中国（分裂行为）
• 反政府工作（颠覆）
• 恐怖主义
• 与其他国家合作对抗中国（与外国实体勾结）
• 背叛国家（叛国）
• 窃取政府机密
• 叛乱色
• 破坏公共基础设施
• １１ 外部干预
2026年3月23日，香港政府修改了有关《香港国家安全法》的实施细则。现在，在国家安全案件中，拒绝向香港警方提供密码或不协助解密以允许当局完全访问所有个人电子设备（包括手机和笔记本电脑）是刑事犯罪。
此法律变更适用于所有在香港的人，包括美国公民，在抵达时或仅在香港国际机场过境时适用。此外，香港政府还有更多的权力来获取和保存他们声称与国家安全犯罪有关的任何个人设备作为证据。
中国将国家安全法适用于香港特区的所有人，包括外国人。中国也可能试图将这些法律适用于不居住在香港的人，包括美国公民和永久居民。
如果您对中国大陆或香港特别行政区提出批评，您可能会被逮捕、拘留、驱逐或起诉。
香港特别行政区当局已对居住在其他国家并涉嫌违反这些法律的人发出逮捕令。这包括居住在其管辖范围之外的美国公民和永久居民。香港特别行政区当局正在向任何提供信息以帮助他们逮捕这些人（如果他们来到香港特别行政区）的人提供现金奖励。
双重国籍
香港特区政府不承认双重国籍。中美双重国籍公民和华裔美国公民可能会受到额外的安全程序和骚扰。如果您是美中双重国籍，并持美国护照进入香港特区，且您被拘留或逮捕，中国当局必须将您的拘留情况通知美国大使馆或美国总领事馆。他们必须允许美国领事官员与您联系。
即使您持有美国护照，美国领事官员也可能无法与您联系。如需了解更多信息，请访问双重国籍人士在香港（特区）的领事保护和居留权–美国驻香港和澳门总领事馆。
示威
根据2020年《香港国家安全法》、2024年《维护国家安全条例》或其他法律规定，参加当局认为构成分裂、颠覆、恐怖主义或与外国勾结行为的示威或其他活动可能导致刑事指控。注意周围环境，避免示威。
